description:
lib.rs:1379-1454 implements OSCAL Profile parameter overrides as a two-phase clone-and-swap: phase 1 resolves every override to (lint_index, param_id) and fails fast on any unknown id; phase 2 clones every targeted lint, applies set_parameter to clones, then swaps clones in only on full success.

Defense: the obvious alternative (mutate registered lints in place, abort on first error) leaves the runner in a partially-updated state when override N+1 rejects. The tests under PKIX-hy2e.6 atomicity_on_invalid_value_keeps_default/keeps_previous_commit lock the correct behavior. A future contributor who tries to 'simplify' by removing the clone-and-swap is wrong — they would reintroduce the partial-state bug under the rationale 'the clone is overhead'.

What a contributor might suggest changing: drop the BTreeMap, mutate lints in place, return on first error. Counter-argument: this is the canonical 'atomic batch update' shape (clone-modify-swap), used in every transactional API from filesystem rename to SQL savepoints. The clone cost is bounded by the size of the override set; for OSCAL Profiles that is a handful per call. Memory cost is documented and acceptable.

Lock this in. Don't let it get refactored away.
title: apply_parameter_overrides clone-and-swap atomicity (PKIX-hy2e.6)
